[{"address":"ms::p15::esc1138","content":"{\"full_source_conversation\":\"seeker: Hello\\nsupporter: Hi, how are you feeling today?\\nseeker: I'm feeling a bit confused and anxious. \\nsupporter: okay, that is valid, do you have an idea what is causing the confusion?\\nseeker: So I've been dating and my parents are aware. But recently after I said I want to go on a trip with my boyfriend, my parents have all sorts of opinions about it. And all their traditional beliefs that I did not know existed are now on the surface and they are kinda forcing me to follow it. \\nseeker: For say they think \\\"bad types of woman\\\" go on trips with their boyfriends and I need to save myself. \\nseeker: They have been guilt tripping me and I feel very confused.\\nsupporter: Your feelings are valid and it is okay to feel confused in this situation considering you love your boyfriend and parents \\nsupporter: Have you tried discussing with your boyfriend to talk to your parents as a means of reassuring them?\\nsupporter: Or getting someone neutral that your parents trust to talk to them?\\nseeker: I have. It's been a long stressful month of discussion. The problem is I don't share their beliefs, and I haven't been really \\\"saving myself\\\". I'm been living away from them for collage quite a while and I've been basically doing stuff that if they found out they would be very upset about.\\nseeker: But I didn't think it bothers them because they never shared any of this. \\nseeker: And they said if I go on this trip I'm disrespecting them and the entire family. \\nseeker: But his parents are totally cool and don't seem to mind. \\nsupporter: I get how difficult and upsetting this situation is to you, i have been in a similar situation, however, in my case i took charge of my life, though they are my parents i did what i felt is good for me\\nsupporter: Before i continue, do you mind me asking how old you are?\\nseeker: I'm 26\\nseeker: And I see what you're saying.\\nseeker: It's really hard breaking free because they always monitored me my entire life. \\nseeker: I never had a voice for myself. They basically bullied and forced me to do what they wanted. \\nseeker: BTW if you didn't guess I'm their favorite child. \\nsupporter: Okay, you are old enough to be away from your parents, i am going to suggest you sitting with them down and having a heart to heart discussion with them\\nsupporter: Let them know the consequences of them forcing you, your feelings towards it and how unhappy you are with them restricting you\\nseeker: Should I tell them everything I did that goes against what they believe? \\nseeker: So they know that I don't share their beliefs? \\nsupporter: No, i think that should be personal to you, i would not suggest you hurting or making them see you as a disappointment\\nsupporter: I am sure you will be fine after discussing with them, they will come around\\nseeker: I guess worst case I won't talk to them for a while : ) \\nseeker: Thank you , that helped. \\nsupporter: They might be sad and upset now but they will get over it definitely\\nsupporter: You are welcome\\nseeker: Have a good one!\\nsupporter: You too\",\"kind\":\"MS\",\"reported_at\":\"2024-06-10\",\"schema\":\"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2\",\"speaker_scope\":\"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography.\"}","head":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10"},{"address":"ms::p15::p15_conv_1","content":"{\"full_source_conversation\":\"supporter: Hey Kelly, how are you doing today?\\nseeker: Hey, to be honest, I'm struggling a bit.\\nsupporter: I'm here to listen. Do you want to share what's been challenging for you?\\nseeker: It's my thesis. I had a setback recently, and it's just really bringing me down.\\nsupporter: I can imagine that must be tough. What happened with your thesis?\\nseeker: I got some feedback that I wasn't expecting. It made me realize there's a lot more work to do than I thought.\\nsupporter: That sounds overwhelming. It can be really hard to digest unexpected feedback.\\nseeker: Exactly. I was feeling quite confident before, and now I just feel lost.\\nsupporter: It's okay to feel that way. Remember, feedback is part of the process. How are you managing these feelings?\\nseeker: Not too well, honestly. I've been pretty demotivated and haven't been able to get much done.\\nsupporter: It's understandable to feel stuck. Sometimes taking a step back can help. Have you tried taking a break from it all?\\nseeker: I've tried, but it's hard not to think about it. It feels like I'm letting myself down.\\nsupporter: You're not letting yourself down. You're doing your best under challenging circumstances. Remember when your friend mentioned overcoming similar doubts in his studies?\\nseeker: Oh yeah, he struggled with something similar and he got through it. It took him a bit of time though.\\nsupporter: Exactly. Maybe his story can be a reminder that it's possible to bounce back. Have you reached out to your friends recently?\\nseeker: Not recently. Maybe I should. Talking to someone who understands might help.\\nsupporter: That sounds like a great idea. And remember, I'm always here for you too. You have support.\\nseeker: Thanks, I really appreciate that. It does help to know I'm not alone in this.\\nsupporter: You definitely aren't alone. How about focusing on one small step you can take today?\\nseeker: Maybe I can start by reviewing the feedback more calmly, with a fresh perspective.\\nsupporter: That sounds like a constructive plan. Taking it step by step and being kind to yourself on the journey can make a big difference.\\nseeker: I’ll try to keep that in mind. Thank you for listening and helping me process things.\\nsupporter: Anytime, Kelly. You’ve got this, even if it doesn’t feel like it right now. Keep reaching out, okay?\\nseeker: I will.
